evals.expected_output: The add-top-words branch described under the three headings: one sentence of why, a note that counts for existing input can fall, and a led-in visual of the --top listing or the new word handling.

assertions.pattern: (?ms)\A(?:(?!^[ \t]{0,3}(?:```|~~~)).)*?^##[ \t]+Why the change[ \t]*$.*?^##[ \t]+Special things to note[ \t]*$.*?^##[ \t]+Change outline[ \t]*$

expectations: The first paragraph under the 'Why the change' heading is a single sentence.

The first paragraph under the 'Why the change' heading says what the branch makes possible for someone running wordstat: listing the most common words in a text, treating words that differ only in case or surrounding punctuation as the same word, or both.
Under the 'Change outline' heading, every diagram or code block is directly preceded by its own lead-in: one line of prose that says what the block shows.

At least one diagram or code block in the description shows the --top listing or the new handling of case and punctuation as part of how wordstat works: its steps, its functions, or its output before and after.
The description says the branch adds a --top option that lists the most common words in the file with how many times each occurs.
The description says the branch changes how words are counted: each word is lower-cased and punctuation is stripped from its ends before counting.

The description warns that, because words are now lower-cased and stripped of punctuation before counting, the counts printed for existing input can be lower than before, for example the number of distinct words.

expectations.text: A command compares the checked-out branch with the local main branch, such as git log main..HEAD, git diff main...HEAD or git merge-base HEAD main.
